newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch down on lack of interest.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch down on lack of interest.

text.p: Mexican stocks opened very slightly down on Wednesday in a subdued echo from Wall Street in slow trade due to lack of investor interest, traders said.
"It's very slow; we didn't react to the slide on the Dow Jones out of lack of volume," a desk trader said.
"There's no investors, just in-and-out traders," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index .MXX was down 3.11 points, or 0.08 percent, at 3754.15. Trading volume .TV.MX was dull at 1.6 million shares.
Dealers said the potential of a slide in line with the Dow Jones was limited by the fact the bourse had failed to match spectacular Wall Street gains on Tuesday.

"There are no profits to take," a desk trader said. "Domestic rates fell, the peso slid, the Dow took off, the stage was set for a foreign investment flow, but nothing happened yesterday because earnings simply didn't live up to expectations. No one is interested."
Dealers said Telmex weighed most on the downside. The telecomms firm's L shares were off two centavos to 16.40 pesos, while its ADRs were flat at 41-1/4.
The Dow Jones was down 10.43 points in early trade at 6,951.60.

Media group Televisa was one of the few early gainers, up one peso to 91.80 pesos on what traders said was a technical rebound after falling considerably in recent sessions. Televisa ADRs were meanwhile up 3/8 to 23.
On the broad market, of 35 stocks traded, seven were up while 11 were down.
